children: Indian benchmark indices are likely to see a positive start on November 16, tracking GIFT Nifty, which is trading higher at 25,218.50 in early trade.
Track the latest updates on GIFT Nifty right here on Moneycontrol
Indian benchmark indices snapped their three-session winning streak and ended lower on November 13, with the Nifty slipping below the 25,200 mark amid broad-based selling across sectors.

Amid mixed global cues, domestic markets opened lower and remained in negative territory for most of the session, with the Nifty hitting an intraday low of 25,054.40. However, buying at lower levels helped the indices recover some of their intraday losses before the close.
At close, the Sensex was down 318.56 points or 0.39 percent at 81,592.45, and the Nifty was down 155.05 points or 0.61 percent at 25,144.30.
For the week BSE Sensex added 0.7 percent and Nfity50 index rose 0.45 percent.
Here is how financial markets across the globe fared overnight:
GIFT Nifty (Up)
GIFT Nifty was trading firm at around 25,218.50 in early trade, indicating a positive start for the domestic equity markets.
Asian Markets (Slip)
Asian equities fell in early trading as investors looked ahead to a busy week that may help shape the near-term outlook for the artificial intelligence trade.

MSCI Inc.’s gauge of Asian shares declined 0.8%. Futures for the Nasdaq 100 and the S&P 500 edged slightly lower, erasing earlier gains after both underlying benchmarks capped a second straight day of losses on Friday.
US Equities (Mixed)

The S&P 500 and Nasdaq closed lower on Friday, as concerns ​about Nvidia pressured technology shares, while a reading on inflation failed to alter expectations for more rate hikes from the Federal Reserve.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 50.46 points, or 0.10%, to 52,347.55, the S&P 500 lost 30.73 points, or 0.40%, to 7,561.67 and the Nasdaq Composite lost 229.82 points, or 0.91%, to 25,136.27.
Dollar Index (Up)

The dollar has been gaining strength against most of its peers after hawkish commentary from Federal Reserve officials and a hot October inflation report, which have revived bets that the US central bank will have to take aggressive action to rein in cost-of-living pressures.
The US dollar index, which measures the greenback's strength against a basket of six currencies, was trading at 103.44, its highest since April 2025.
US Bond Yield (Up)
The yield on 10-year Treasuries was little changed at 5.14%, while 2-year Treasury bond were up 2 basis points at 4.86%.
Asian currencies (Mixed)

Asian currencies traded on a mixed note against the US dollar, with the Indonesian rupiah emerging as the top gainer, rising 0.18 percent, followed by the Malaysian ringgit, which strengthened 0.06 percent, and the Thai baht, up 0.04 percent. The South Korean won and Singapore dollar also posted marginal gains of 0.03 percent and 0.06 percent, respectively.

On the other hand, the Taiwan dollar weakened the most, declining 0.12 percent, followed by the Philippine peso, which fell 0.08 percent, and the Singapore dollar, down 0.06 percent. The Japanese yen and Chinese renminbi also edged lower by 0.06 percent and 0.01 percent, respectively.
Crude (Down)
Oil steadied after a two-week slump, as fresh attacks in the Middle East countered signs of a well- supplied physical market.
Brent held near $96 a barrel after falling more than 2% last week, while West Texas Intermediate was above $88.
Gold (Down)
Gold steadied after its worst week since June, with traders looking to a flurry of Federal Reserve speakers and the central bank’s latest policy minutes for clues on the outlook for interest rates.
Bullion was near $3,890 an ounce, having tumbled 4.6% in the previous week.
Fund Flow Action

Foreign institutional investors (FIIs) extended their buying streak to the fourth consecutive session, purchasing equities worth Rs 5,736 crore on November 13. Meanwhile, domestic institutional investors (DIIs) continued their selling for the 11th consecutive session, offloading equities worth Rs 2,253 crore.
